Subject: Exec approval request: cancellation trigger + tiered ramp schedule for Brightline Health (DEAL-2026-1472)

Hi Marissa / Marcus —

Short ask: Brightline has pushed back on our standard early-termination language and requested a 60-day convenience termination with a tiered ramp/"downsell protection" schedule and a concession on year-1 list pricing (they're asking 25%). Sales has negotiated to the terms below; I need exec approval to accept the non-standard clauses so we can close this week.

Summary of proposal we negotiated with customer:
- Early termination: Customer may terminate for convenience with 60 days' written notice.
- Tiered ramp / downsell protection (to limit revenue cliff): if Customer terminates within first 12 months, Redwood will apply the following credits to outstanding invoices as an accommodation: months 1–3: 100% of committed MRR applies (no credit), months 4–6: 75% applies (25% credit), months 7–12: 50% applies (50% credit). After month 12, no credit.
- Pricing concession: 20% off list for year 1 (back to standard year-2 pricing).
- Limited condition: clause only allowed for this enterprise account, non-precedential, and will auto-expire if Customer expands to Dedicated by contract amendment.

Why: Brightline is a strategic healthcare win (pilot -> enterprise) and procurement is pressing on early-termination protection; they will walk without this. Our alternatives are to hold firm (likely lose) or to accept the schedule above plus additional guardrails.

Risks I want you to consider:
- Revenue recognition complexity & potential billing credits; finance will want the commitments mapped to revenue schedules.
- Precedent risk for other enterprise deals if we publish the language.
- Operational: CS onboarding cost if they downscale rapidly; need to lock minimum notice and deprovision schedule.

Attachments: Brightline_SOW_redline_v3.pdf (redlines include the proposed opt-out clause), pricing_matrix_tiered_ramp.xlsx (shows net ARR impact under several churn scenarios).

Requested approvals (yes/no + any edits):
1) Accept the 60-day convenience termination with the tiered ramp credits as written above?
2) Approve a 20% year-1 discount (net of any one-time onboarding credits).
3) Sign off on marking the clause "non-precedential" and limiting to this account unless Business Development asks for a precedent exception in writing.

Timing: Brightline expects final redline back by EOD Wednesday (10/07) to meet their procurement cycle.

Thanks —
Rishi

All —

Reviewed the redline. Below is suggested contract language for the SOW amendment (clean copy for your legal/finance teams):

--- proposed clause (to be inserted as Section 8.2 in SOW) ---
Customer Termination for Convenience: Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Redwood. In the event of such termination within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Redwood will apply the following ramp protections to committed Monthly Recurring Revenue ("MRR") for the purpose of calculating any invoice adjustments or credits: (i) Months 1–3: 100% of committed MRR remains billable and collectible; (ii) Months 4–6: 75% of committed MRR remains billable and collectible; (iii) Months 7–12: 50% of committed MRR remains billable and collectible. No ramp protection applies after month twelve. Any credits due under this section will be recorded as a contra-revenue liability and amortized in accordance with Redwood's revenue recognition policy.

Conditions and limitations: (a) This provision is expressly non-precedential and may not be cited by Customer as a basis for any future concession absent Redwood's written executive approval. (b) This provision applies only to the Customer named in this Agreement and terminates automatically if Customer executes a Dedicated Capacity Amendment. (c) Any request for a longer or deeper ramp schedule will require Executive Committee approval and written documentation of strategic rationale.

Comments:
- Replace "apply credits to outstanding invoices" language in the redline with the more precise accounting treatment clause above (helps Finance).
- Add a defined process for dispute resolution on any calculation of credits (AR + CS involvement).
- I can incorporate these into the redline and send final PDF to procurement if Marcus confirms finance treatment.

Marcus — can you confirm finance is comfortable with the amortization / liability handling?

Karthik
